test_conditions.thermal_history: arc melting followed by hot isostatic press

mechanisms.assertion: RHEAs retain good yield strength at high temperatures

evidence_spans: Senkov et al. [18] first reported two RHEAs, MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW by arc melting followed by a hot isostatic press. Both RHEAs are single-phase alloys with a body-centered cubic structure and retain good yield strength at high temperatures of 600–1600 °C. Remarkably, the yield strength of MoNbTaVW at 1000 °C reaches 842 MPa, which is significantly higher than that of Ni-based superalloys Inconel 718 and Mar-M247 that are used as high-temperature parts on jet turbine engines. However, both MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW exhibit poor room-temperature fracture toughness and high density.

mechanisms.assertion: Replacing heavy elements with lighter elements improves room temperature ductility

evidence_spans: Thus, Senkov et al. [18] explored the possibility of replacing heavy elements W, Mo and Ta with lighter elements Ti, Hf and Zr and successfully obtained HfNbTaTiZr RHEAs, which also have a BCC crystal structure. HfNbTaTiZr possesses outstanding room temperature ductility ( ε > 50%) and considerable strain hardening and its yield strength reaches 929 MPa. Intriguingly, its yield strength at elevated temperature (1000 °C) is poor, which is only 295 MPa.

mechanisms.assertion: Replacing Nb with Mo enhances strength at both room and high temperatures

evidence_spans: Thus, Juan et al. [20] replaced Nb in HfNbTaTiZr with Mo. It is encouraging that the obtained as-cast HfMoTaTiZr RHEA shows high strength at both room temperature (1600 MPa) and high temperature (855 MPa), which is great progress compared with MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW. Nonetheless, HfMoTaTiZr has a relatively high density, 10.21 g cm −3 .

process_steps.action: replacing Nb, Ti and Zr with Cr

mechanisms.assertion: Cr alloying in bcc RHEAs strengthens the alloys

evidence_spans: Wang et al. [28] replaced Nb, Ti and Zr, respectively, with Cr and observed that a Laves phase emerged regardless of which element was substituted by Cr and a significant enhancement in strength was achieved in all cases. Similar phenomena were also observed by Fazakas et al. [29] (TiZrHfNbCr) and Yan et al. [30] (WMoNbTiCr).

The shape of the (200), (211) and (220) peaks are asymmetric due to the compositional difference between dendrite and interdendrite regions.
The XRD-determined lattice parameters of HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 are a HfMoTaTiZr = 3.392 Å and a HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 = 3.325 Å, respectively.
The same as the lattice parameters, the density of HfMoTaTiZr is also higher than that measured by Juan et al. [20] and the theoretical density ( Table 2 ).
Table 3 summarises the EDS-determined fraction and compositions of the dendritic and interdendritic regions of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 RHEAs.
The Vickers hardness of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 RHEAs at room temperature are also measured in the study.

The yield strength ( σ 0.2 ) of HfMoTaTiZr in this work is 1543.1 ± 40.9 MPa, which is consistent with that in ref. [20] (1600 MPa). However, the fracture strain ( ε f ) of present HfMoTaTiZr reaches 11.6%, 65.5% higher than that of Juan et al. [20] Considering the observation by XRD, it is speculated that the improved ductility or ε f of HfMoTaTiZr is attributed to the slight compositional difference from that of Juan et al. [20]

evidence_spans: Fig. 1 shows the X-ray diffraction patterns of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZr 0.5 . ... In addition to the diffraction peaks of the BCC phase, peaks corresponding to the Laves phase are also observed.
The XRD-determined lattice parameters of HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 are a HfMoTaTiZr = 3.392 Å and a HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 = 3.325 Å, respectively.
The addition of 4.2 at% Cr effectively increases the hardness from HfMoTaTiZr 460.1 HV 0.3 to 535.8 HV 0.3 , increased by 16.5%.
The σ 0.2 and ε f of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 reach 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa and 14.0 ± 2.9%, respectively, which are 207.5 MPa and 20.6% higher than those of the present HfMoTaTiZr

First, XRD analysis indicates that a certain amount of Cr was dissolved in the BCC phase of HfMoTaTiZr. Cr also has the smallest atom radius among constitute elements of HfMoTaTiZr. Thus, incorporating Cr into the existing BCC unit cell will lead to more severe lattice distortions and more dislocations, i.e. , solid solution hardening

Secondly, the presence of the intermetallic phase and its dispersion can also affect the hardness and compressive strength. ... The Cr addition in this work leads to the formation of a hard intermetallic Laves phase, which has a positive impact on the hardness and strength of HfMoTaTiZr.

However, in the as-cast HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 , the Laves phase is connected and forms a reticulated structure. Such a unique structure is expected to hinder crack propagation during deformation and compensate for the loss in plasticity caused by the formation of the brittle Laves phase.
